summary.text: April McClain Delaney is the Democratic U.S. Representative for Maryland's 6th Congressional District, elected in 2024 to succeed David Trone, and won re-election on November 3, 2026.
A communications lawyer, she worked for a children-and-technology nonprofit and, from 2022, at the U.S. Department of Commerce under President Biden before her election.

paragraphs.text: McClain Delaney was born in Buhl, Idaho, in 1964, and according to her congressional website grew up there as the daughter of a potato farmer.
She earned a bachelor's degree in communications from Northwestern University in 1986 and a law degree from Georgetown Law Center in 1989.

McClain Delaney began her career in communications law with the satellite firm Orion Network Systems and later became Washington director for Common Sense Media, a nonprofit focused on children and technology.

In 2022 she joined the U.S. Department of Commerce as deputy assistant secretary for communications and information at the National Telecommunications and Information Administration (NTIA); according to her website, her work there included broadband access and digital equity efforts and the First Responder Network.
She has also served on the boards of the Georgetown University Law Center, the International Center for Research on Women, and the Northwestern University School of Communications.
McClain Delaney won the 2024 general election for Maryland's 6th District with 53.0% of the vote over Republican Neil Parrott and took office on January 3, 2025, as the successor to David Trone.

In the House she serves on the Committee on Agriculture (subcommittees on Commodity Markets, Digital Assets, and Rural Development, and on Conservation, Research, and Biotechnology) and the Committee on Science, Space, and Technology (Research and Technology subcommittee).
She advanced from the June 23, 2026 Democratic primary and, according to her website, lives in Montgomery County with her husband, former Rep. John Delaney, and their four children.
She won the November 3, 2026 general election with 58.4% of the vote to Robin Ficker's 38.9% and Moshe Landman's 2.7%, according to unofficial results reported by NBC News.
